body: [{"streamId":"01a0f96f-9ec1-7401-8f4e-44db5f6b4783","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0f96f-9ec1-7401-8f4e-44db5f6b4783\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022A mention seen by a teammate\\u0027s install never claims or launches on a task assigned to another owner\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022AutoPrReviewEngine\\u0027s mention attach applies the same owner-root rule the CLI task commands use (TaskOwnerRule), and does not claim or dispatch a mention follow-up on a task whose assigned root is not this node owner\\u0027s root\u0022,\u0022A test reproduces the #2166 case: a teammate\\u0027s install sees a mention of its own login on a pull request whose pr-review task belongs to another owner, and no TaskClaimed or run results on either node\u0022,\u0022A daemon-originated mention claim on another owner\\u0027s task is refused even when this install\\u0027s owner holds the Owner role; the Owner-role override stays a human act with a stated reason (h9k task abandon --holder --reason and its siblings), and this ruling is recorded in the decisions log (Brian, 2026-10-02)\u0022,\u0022A mention on a pull request whose only covering task belongs to another owner gets a row for this install\\u0027s owner and never mints a new pr-review task (Brian, 2026-10-02)\u0022,\u0022The review-request side\\u0027s covering-task lookup (AutoPrReviewEngine.cs around 897) is owner-scoped the same way: a teammate\\u0027s live pr-review task on the same pull request never makes a review request to this owner read as already covered, and a test shows this owner\\u0027s review is minted in that case\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022The mention path claims and launches on a task without asking whose task it is. AutoPrReviewEngine.AttachMentionAsync finds the covering task by the pull request\\u0027s external reference alone (AutoPrReviewEngine.cs:2067-2076). Its gates (2241-2380) never look at the assignee or owner root. TaskDecider.ClaimForMentionFollowUp (TaskDecider.cs:2280) documents that it does no owner identity check. The v0.11.3 owner-root rule (TaskOwnerRule, 5bacf6fa1/95e7e900b/baef0c975) is applied only in CLI commands, never in the daemon. The receive gate (EventReplicationInbox.EvaluateTaskActVerdict, v0.11.0) protects only the receiving ledger and always lets an Owner-role sender\\u0027s act through, so it cannot stop a teammate\\u0027s node from claiming and launching on its own machine.\\n\\nShape to weigh: apply the same TaskOwnerRule the CLI uses at the attach and claim seam. A teammate\\u0027s mention that lands on another owner\\u0027s task should be recorded (or routed to that teammate as their own item) without a claim. The Owner-role pass-through never covers a daemon-originated claim on another owner\\u0027s task: Brian ruled this at the walk (2026-10-02), following his 2026-10-01 cross-owner ruling that an Owner-role override happens only on an explicit human ask with a reason.\\n\\n## Motivating case: AgelessRx/arx-platform#2166, pr-review task bc7d2572 (2026-10-01 EDT)\\n\\n- bc7d2572 is Brian\\u0027s (Hallmanac) pr-review task for #2166, scope Team, assigned to Brian Hall. It had been parked merge-ready since about noon.\\n- 11:49 Taylor Dennison (taylor-dennison) asked a question on the PR.\\n- 17:21:23 Brian replied as Hallmanac, mentioning @taylor-dennison (issue comment 5940862269). The comment answered Taylor; nothing in it was for Brian.\\n- 17:23 feed: \\u0022bc7d2572 claimed by TaylorDenny as a deliberate kick-off; a run is starting\\u0022. Taylor\\u0027s install had a real mention of its own login, found Brian\\u0027s replicated task by external reference with no owner filter, and claimed it through TaskDecider.ClaimForMentionFollowUp. That claim carries the empty node id, so the feed (OrchestratorFeedDescription.cs:124-125) labelled it a deliberate kick-off. That label is wrong.\\n- 17:26 feed: \\u0022bc7d2572 claimed by node ef6ab27d\\u0022. The order here is inferred from the code: Taylor\\u0027s safe pre-flight requeued the task with PendingMentionFollowUpAfterPreflight (RunSupervisor.cs:352-357), still assigned to Brian. Brian\\u0027s dispatcher claimed it and took the pending-follow-up branch (RunLauncher.cs:163-180).\\n- 17:27 parked with a mention-followup addendum, run 01a0f95c-a4cc-7362-a7c8-bfd6ba613d3a, reading \\u0022Tagged by Hallmanac\\u0022. The session found no question for Brian and drafted nothing.\\n\\nEvidence comes from a code trace at v0.11.3 (e03c7d7e6). Mention match and self-author filter: src/Hall9k.Connectors/WorkItems/GitHubReviewAssignments.cs:439-440, 482-484. Attach: src/Hall9k.Daemon/AutoPrReview/AutoPrReviewEngine.cs:2058-2409, with the covering-task lookup at 2067-2076. Receive gate: src/Hall9k.Connectors/Replication/EventReplicationInbox.cs:2013, Owner-role pass-through around 2045-2048.\\n\\n\\n## Added 2026-10-02 (Brian, f894d344 discovery questions 2 and 3)\\n\\nCriterion four is the discovery\\u0027s decision-order step 3 (notes/discovery-f894d344-2026-10-01/report.md in the project home): for #2166 it gives Taylor a row reading that Hallmanac mentioned taylor-dennison, and gives Brian\\u0027s board nothing. Criterion five folds in the request-side sibling, a code-reading finding with no observed incident: scope.md says a teammate\\u0027s review of the same pull request is a different owner\\u0027s work and is never touched. Both lookups should share one owner-scoped helper rather than two copies of the rule.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-02T14:12:31.241789\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Effort\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"f755af11-14d7-4d81-9b96-3116a25ce9f8","originSequence":85179,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-02T14:12:31.252637+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
